description:
Production mutation contexts are constructed through one factory instead of twenty-three
independent constructor calls spread across fourteen command modules and one
integration-test helper, with behaviour unchanged.

## Background

The production mutation context — the injected authority and clock a finalized plan derives
its identifiers and timestamp from — is constructed independently wherever a command needs
one. A fact decided once at dispatch has no way to reach those contexts without either
threading through the modules one by one or converging their construction first. Convergence
is the shared-convention remedy: one factory owns production-context construction and carries
an optional dispatch-scoped annotation slot, empty by default, so a later change can set a
fact in one place and have it reach the finalizer through the context it already receives.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One factory constructs the production mutation context, the per-module constructor calls and the integration-test helper route through it, and the direct constructor is no longer callable from command modules or integration tests.
- [hard] REQ-02: The factory carries an optional dispatch-scoped annotation slot that is empty by default, and an empty slot changes no behaviour: no new events, identical outputs, identical persisted bytes for the same inputs.
- [hard] REQ-03: The full test suite passes unchanged apart from construction-site mechanics, demonstrating the convergence is behaviour-preserving.
title: Converge mutation-context construction onto one factory
